analysis: The trial succeeded with host-measured macro validation HR@10 of 0.6200, improving over 0.6075 by 0.0125 (1.25 percentage points). Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.675, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.600, Electronics 0.495, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.710. Electronics improved from the reported 0.430 baseline. These results support retaining the 16-negative cross-entropy experiment, although one seeded trial does not establish general robustness or causality. Allocated GPU time was 519.65 seconds. No test performance was reported.
code_summary: Preserved independent per-category MultVAE and SASRec models with equal-weight fusion of candidate ranks. MultVAE uses uniform normalized binary histories, a 256-unit encoder, 64-dimensional latent representation, full-catalog reconstruction, and annealed KL loss. SASRec retains two causal attention blocks, 50-dimensional embeddings, sequence length 50, one attention head, and dropout 0.5. Its training objective now scores each active positive against 16 uniform negatives sampled with replacement, excluding the user's complete training history, using 17-way cross-entropy. Negative embeddings are gathered only at active positions. Training seed 42, four-category routing, checkpoint selection, saved configurations, and generated predictor loading remain preserved.
